title: Newt kidney tubules keep normal diameter with fewer, larger cells, down to one cell

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Newt kidney tubules keep normal diameter with fewer, larger cells, down to one cell

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In newts whose embryonic cells are made larger (e.g. by polyploidy), kidney tubules use fewer cells to keep the normal tubule diameter and body size, and with enormous cells a single cell bends around itself to form the tubule, showing that different molecular mechanisms are called on to reach the same large-scale anatomical goal.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: However, if the cells of the early embryo are artificially made to be larger, fewer cells will be used, resulting in the same (normal) tubule diameter and overall body size. Remarkably, this can be pushed to a fascinating extreme: if the cells are made to be enormous, a single cell will bend around itself, producing the normal size tubule diameter.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity”. Scope: Polyploid newt embryos (Fankhauser 1945)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The anatomical quantities have clear decision criteria, but the evidential base is an old, narrow experiment. Public reports can check the reported pattern but not support a strong modern reanalysis of variability or mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate ploidy and cell cross-sectional area to cell count and lumen diameter in archived newt kidney sections, testing whether diameter remains normal even at the one-cell extreme.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Modern raw histology and biological replicates are unlikely to be public.

The 1945 study may provide only published images and summary measurements.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell number, cell size and tubule diameter are standard variables, and the classic paper reports the compensation down to a single curved cell. Those measurements are not in any open repository, so a check means recovering mid-century plates rather than running a deposited table. The anatomical pattern can be scrutinized from that literature; the further claim that different molecular pathways are recruited to meet a goal is not in those plates.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In polyploid versus diploid newt embryos, count cells per pronephric-tubule cross-section, measure cell cross-sectional area, and measure lumen diameter, including the extreme in which one cell forms the wall. Matched diameter with fewer, larger cells would support size compensation; diameter scaling in proportion to cell size, or no single-cell tubules, would refute that part. Calling the match a switch among molecular mechanisms, or an anatomical goal, needs a separate assay the anatomy does not contain.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cell size was changed by ploidy, which also changes nuclear content, so mechanism switching is not isolated.

The counts and drawings are in a 1945 journal article and later retellings, not a downloadable table or image stack.

The sample is newt pronephric tubules, not kidney tubules in general.
